items.stem: What problem does retrieval (file search) solve for an LLM application?

options.text: It grounds responses in your own documents instead of relying only on the model's training
options.rationale: Correct: retrieval supplies relevant source text so answers are grounded.

options.text: It makes the model respond faster in every case
options.rationale: Retrieval adds a lookup step; speed is not its purpose.

options.text: It removes the need to verify any answer
options.rationale: Grounded answers still require verification against sources.
Retrieval does not remove token costs.

items.explanation: Correct: retrieval supplies relevant source text so answers are grounded.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Why is chunking documents (rather than indexing each whole document) important for file search?

options.text: Smaller, well-bounded chunks let retrieval return the precise relevant passage
options.rationale: Correct: good chunks improve retrieval precision.

options.text: It permanently reduces the number of documents
options.rationale: Chunking splits content; it does not reduce the document set.
Citations remain important regardless of chunking.

options.text: It guarantees the model never makes an error
options.rationale: Chunking improves retrieval but does not guarantee correctness.

items.explanation: Correct: good chunks improve retrieval precision.

items.stem: Which TWO practices improve the reliability of a retrieval application? (Select TWO)

options.text: Show citations to the source passages used
options.rationale: Correct: citations let users verify grounded answers.

options.text: Evaluate retrieval against question and expected-source pairs
options.rationale: Correct: evaluation measures whether the right sources are found.

options.text: Pass every retrieved chunk to the model regardless of relevance
options.rationale: Irrelevant chunks add noise and cost.

options.text: Trust any confident answer even when no source is returned
options.rationale: A confident answer with no source is a failure mode, not reliability.

items.explanation: Correct: citations let users verify grounded answers.
